title: Tech Note: Active Directory - Single Sign-on Using 4D 2004
author: Thomas Maul, General Manager, 4D Germany.

historical_commentary.text: This note demonstrates a clever no-plug-in workaround for Active Directory single sign-on by shelling out to a dynamically generated VBScript via LAUNCH EXTERNAL PROCESS, a very much of-its-era technique for a Windows-only 4D 2004 application. The general problem it solves (mapping AD/LDAP users and groups into 4D's internal password system) remains conceptually relevant, but the implementation is thoroughly obsolete: it predates 4D's SQL engine (introduced in v11, 2007), predates Project Mode and ORDA by over a decade, and relies on legacy commands and a VBScript-shelling approach that modern 4D developers would replace with built-in LDAP/network commands or a proper external component/plug-in.
related_updates: Later 4D versions added more direct commands for external process/network interaction, reducing reliance on hand-rolled VBScript shelling
4D v11 (2007) introduced 4D's native SQL engine, unrelated to this note's topic but marking the broader platform evolution since this note's publication
Modern 4D authentication integrations more commonly use LDAP libraries, REST/OAuth, or dedicated plug-ins rather than shelling out to VBScript
